events.title: BASIC runs for the first time at Dartmouth
events.summary: Kemeny and Kurtz ran the first BASIC programs on the Dartmouth Time-Sharing System at 4 a.m. on May 1, 1964.
events.about: BASIC (Beginner's All-Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code) let students and non-specialists write programs with simple English-like commands (`PRINT`, `LET`, `IF`). It spread through the Apple II, Commodore 64, and IBM PC era — millions learned to code in classroom and hobby BASIC before the web existed.

narrative.whyChosen: BASIC democratized programming the way VB later democratized Windows apps — simple syntax, immediate feedback.
narrative.whyImportant: Paired with time-sharing, it proved that computing could be interactive and accessible, not just batch jobs for specialists.
narrative.problemSolved: Students queued for batch runs on mainframes; Dartmouth needed a language anyone could learn in hours on a terminal.
